subject: Materials Science
title: Crystal Lattices in Metals
description: A short lesson to help you apply Crystal Lattices in Metals.

hook.text: Metal atoms don't sit in random piles. They line up in precise 3D grids.

buildup.text: These repeating arrangements are called crystal lattices — order at atomic scale.

discovery.text: Most metals choose one of three lattice types: BCC, FCC, or HCP.

twist.text: The lattice type decides properties — FCC metals are ductile, BCC metals are strong.

climax.text: Iron switches from BCC to FCC when heated, completely changing its behavior.

punchline.text: A metal's personality starts with how its atoms stack.

quiz.question: What are the three main crystal lattice types in metals?
